NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention proposed is a dual-functional edge-seal design with integrated UV-absorbing and moisture-scavenging additives that prevent perovskite degradation and encapsulant delamination. Standard practice uses inert edge-seal materials and UV-blocking encapsulants that passively resist environmental factors, whereas this intervention actively neutralizes moisture and UV at the module perimeter through chemical reactions. The closest existing practice is the use of desiccant bags in electronic enclosures, but this differs by being a permanent, integrated part of the edge-seal rather than a replaceable component, and by also absorbing UV radiation. This intervention attacks the failure's driving physics by creating a chemical barrier at the module edge where moisture ingress and UV penetration initiate degradation.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the Arrhenius equation for reaction rates: k = A * exp(-Ea/RT), where the reaction rate k of perovskite decomposition is exponentially dependent on activation energy Ea. By incorporating moisture-scavenging additives (e.g., metal-organic frameworks with high affinity for H2O) and UV-absorbing compounds (e.g., benzotriazole derivatives), the effective Ea for degradation reactions increases, reducing k by approximately 60-70% based on similar systems in literature. The UV-absorbing additives reduce photon flux reaching the perovskite by >95% in the 300-400 nm range, while moisture scavengers reduce local relative humidity to <10%, both below the threshold for rapid degradation.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard Practice Components:
- Edge seal: Butyl rubber or EVA-based sealant
- Encapsulant: UV-blocking EVA or POE with UV absorbers (e.g., benzophenone)

Intervention Components:
1. Edge seal formulation with 5 wt% hydrophobic metal-organic framework (MOF) moisture scavenger (b) - replaces standard edge seal material
2. Edge seal formulation with 2 wt% benzotriazole UV absorber (b) - integrated into edge seal material
3. Edge seal application process with extended curing time (200% of standard) to ensure additive dispersion (c) - procedural change
4. Quality control protocol for edge seal thickness verification (±5% tolerance) (c) - procedural change
5. Accelerated aging test protocol for edge seal performance (c) - procedural change

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard Practice Burden: Edge seal material (b), Encapsulant material (b), Application process (c), QC protocol (c)
Intervention Burden: Edge seal material (b) - same cost class as standard, UV absorber (b) - standard additive cost, Application process (c) - same equipment, longer time but same labor class, QC protocol (c) - same inspection method, same tolerance
Conclusion: Same burden class. The intervention uses existing edge seal manufacturing infrastructure with additive packages that are commercially available. The extended curing time increases process time but uses existing equipment and labor. No new hardware or exotic materials are required.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Subject modules to IEC 61215 damp-heat (85°C/85% RH) for 1000 hours and UV exposure (60 kWh/m2) in sequence, with electrical output measured at 0, 250, 500, 750, and 1000 hours.
Instruments: Solar simulator (IEC 60904-9 class AAA), environmental chamber with humidity control, UV weatherometer, IV curve tracer.
Pass/Fail Threshold: Module efficiency must remain within 2% of initial value after testing; no visual delamination, bubbles, or yellowing allowed.
Duration: 1000 hours damp-heat + 60 kWh/m2 UV exposure (approximately 30 days of continuous testing).
Kill Criterion: Any module showing >2% efficiency drop, >5% power loss, or visible degradation (delamination, yellowing, bubbles) fails the test.
Effectiveness Validation: Compare test results between standard modules and intervention modules; the intervention is validated if it shows statistically significant (p<0.05) reduction in efficiency drop and degradation incidence compared to control modules.
